blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-verified 2026-08-09 at Movement ledger_version 192151559 (block_height 83362507); the 2026-07-14 inherited verdict stands with a stronger token-local record. The deployed usdcx module exposes no holder-selective freeze, blacklist, denylist, or seizure entry point, and its paused asserts gate only mint and burn_internal, so the module never sits on holder-to-holder fungible-asset transfers; a TransferRef is generated and stored in usdcx::Management but no function uses it. The local surface is not immutable: the circle_remote package (module usdcx) carries upgrade_policy 1 (compatible) at upgrade_number 0 and its ObjectCore owner is Movement-native multisig 0x98ebb7985c84a89972022edf391bdaa7d95f061d9742efb3703de368413431e1, re-read as 0x1::multisig_account::MultisigAccount with 4 required signatures over 6 owners and no timelock, so holder controls could be added by upgrade. The dominant, named exposure is still upstream: USDCx is issued 1:1 against USDC locked in Circle's xReserve, the sole reserve slice is usdc-circle at 100%, and usdc-circle's own review is reviewedStatus true (Circle holder blacklist). The honest end-state therefore remains inherited over usdc-circle rather than a token-local possible verdict, which would drop the named upstream failure domain without adding any live control.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USDCx is an issuer-native Circle xReserve burn/mint representation on Movement, not an independently canonical Movement-native issuance deployment. The reviewed route binds Ethereum USDC domain 0 to Movement domain 10005; xReserve collateral, RemoteDomainDepositor attestations, and Movement attester/admin/package controls are represented in route-scoped Bridge Risk controls. The current collateral balance and Movement supply are not exact equality proof, and the route remains issuer-native-burn-mint.
